gdep-01-c1.text: Stephen D. Norton. Geologist Richard Oldham's 1906 Paper on Seismic Wave Transmission Establishes the Existence of Earth's Core and Demonstrates the Value of Seismology for Studying the Structure of Earth's Deep Interior. Science and Its Times (Encyclopedia.com).
gdep-01-c1.quote: This was realized in 1889 when Ernst von Rebeur-Paschwitz (1861-1895) demonstrated that seismometers in Germany had detected vibrations that had passed through Earth's interior from an earthquake that had occurred in Tokyo.
gdep-01-c1.claim: In 1889 Ernst von Rebeur-Paschwitz showed that instruments in Germany had picked up vibrations from an earthquake in Tokyo.

gdep-01-c1.text: Stephen D. Norton. Geologist Richard Oldham's 1906 Paper on Seismic Wave Transmission Establishes the Existence of Earth's Core and Demonstrates the Value of Seismology for Studying the Structure of Earth's Deep Interior. Science and Its Times (Encyclopedia.com).
gdep-01-c1.quote: In his landmark report on the 1897 Assam, India, earthquake, Richard Oldham provided the first clear evidence for P-waves, S-waves, and surface waves (1899).
gdep-01-c1.claim: In his 1899 report on the great Assam earthquake of 1897 he gave the first clear evidence for the three main kinds of seismic wave

gdep-01-c1.text: Stephen D. Norton. Geologist Richard Oldham's 1906 Paper on Seismic Wave Transmission Establishes the Existence of Earth's Core and Demonstrates the Value of Seismology for Studying the Structure of Earth's Deep Interior. Science and Its Times (Encyclopedia.com).
gdep-01-c1.quote: Because seismometers located on the other side of Earth from the earthquake detected P-waves later than expected, Oldham concluded Earth must have a central core
gdep-01-c1.claim: At stations on the far side of the Earth, P-waves arrived later than expected.

gdep-01-c1.text: Stephen D. Norton. Geologist Richard Oldham's 1906 Paper on Seismic Wave Transmission Establishes the Existence of Earth's Core and Demonstrates the Value of Seismology for Studying the Structure of Earth's Deep Interior. Science and Its Times (Encyclopedia.com).
gdep-01-c1.quote: He did not however, as is widely believed, discover the core to be liquid.
gdep-01-c1.claim: He did not, as is often believed, show that the core is liquid.

gdep-01-c2.text: Jeroen Ritsema, Vedran Lekić (2020). Heterogeneity of Seismic Wave Velocity in Earth's Mantle. Annual Review of Earth and Planetary Sciences.
gdep-01-c2.quote: the core-mantle boundary (CMB) at a depth of 2,891 km
gdep-01-c2.claim: Modern models put it at 2,891 km, so his figure was remarkably good.

gdep-01-c2.text: Stephen D. Norton. Geologist Richard Oldham's 1906 Paper on Seismic Wave Transmission Establishes the Existence of Earth's Core and Demonstrates the Value of Seismology for Studying the Structure of Earth's Deep Interior. Science and Its Times (Encyclopedia.com).
gdep-01-c2.quote: He reviewed six methods for calculating core rigidity and concluded that all but one clearly indicated a solid core.
gdep-01-c2.claim: He reviewed six methods for estimating its rigidity, and five of them seemed to demand a solid core.

gdep-01-c2.text: Stephen D. Norton. Geologist Richard Oldham's 1906 Paper on Seismic Wave Transmission Establishes the Existence of Earth's Core and Demonstrates the Value of Seismology for Studying the Structure of Earth's Deep Interior. Science and Its Times (Encyclopedia.com).
gdep-01-c2.quote: His most conclusive demonstration was to show that the average mantle rigidity was much greater than the average rigidity of the entire Earth, thus requiring a compensating region of lower rigidity below the mantle.
gdep-01-c2.claim: Jeffreys showed that the mantle is much more rigid than the Earth as a whole, so something below the mantle must be far less rigid to bring the average down.

gdep-01-c3.text: Allison Mills (2015). March 29, 1936: Notes on Earth's Inner Core. EARTH Magazine.
gdep-01-c3.quote: The locations of her seismograph stations — opposite several earthquake hot spots — granted Lehmann unique insight into how earthquake waves traveled great distances.
gdep-01-c3.claim: Her stations sat opposite several earthquake hot spots, which gave her an unusual view of waves that had crossed the core.

gdep-01-c3.text: Allison Mills (2015). March 29, 1936: Notes on Earth's Inner Core. EARTH Magazine.
gdep-01-c3.quote: Two seismograph stations recorded unusually large P-wave amplitudes, although they each were squarely within the shadow zone.
gdep-01-c3.claim: Instead two stations squarely inside the shadow recorded unusually large P-wave amplitudes.

gdep-01-c3.text: Stephen D. Norton. Geologist Richard Oldham's 1906 Paper on Seismic Wave Transmission Establishes the Existence of Earth's Core and Demonstrates the Value of Seismology for Studying the Structure of Earth's Deep Interior. Science and Its Times (Encyclopedia.com).
gdep-01-c3.quote: She calculated the boundary radius to be 870 miles (1,400 km)

gdep-01-c3.text: Stephen D. Norton. Geologist Richard Oldham's 1906 Paper on Seismic Wave Transmission Establishes the Existence of Earth's Core and Demonstrates the Value of Seismology for Studying the Structure of Earth's Deep Interior. Science and Its Times (Encyclopedia.com).

gdep-02-c2.claim: Some slabs appear to lie flat above the 660 km boundary, as beneath Izu-Bonin and Honshu, while others, such as the Marianas and Aegean slabs, have crossed it.

gdep-02-c2.text: Jeroen Ritsema, Vedran Lekić (2020). Heterogeneity of Seismic Wave Velocity in Earth's Mantle. Annual Review of Earth and Planetary Sciences.

gdep-02-c2.claim: In 2013 Fukao and Obayashi argued for a third group, including Java, Kermadec and Peru, that stalls above about 1,000 km depth.

gdep-02-c2.text: Jeroen Ritsema, Vedran Lekić (2020). Heterogeneity of Seismic Wave Velocity in Earth's Mantle. Annual Review of Earth and Planetary Sciences.
gdep-02-c2.quote: At 1,500- and 2,800-km depth, the high-velocity structures are the remnants of the Tethys, Farallon, and Mongol-Okhotsk slabs of oceanic lithosphere that subducted into the mantle in the Permian period and the Mesozoic era.
gdep-02-c2.claim: At 1,500 and 2,800 km depth, fast structures mark the remains of the Tethys, Farallon and Mongol-Okhotsk slabs, oceanic plates that subducted in the Permian and the Mesozoic.

gdep-05-c2.text: Kevin Burke, Trond H. Torsvik, Pavel V. gdep-05-c3.text: G. R. Foulger (2007). The “Plate” model for the genesis of melting anomalies. Geophysical Research Abstracts (EGU General Assembly 2007).
gdep-05-c3.quote: It postulates that volcanism occurs where the lithosphere is in extension, and that the volume of melt produced is related primarily to the fertility of the source material tapped.
gdep-05-c3.claim: volcanism occurs where the lithosphere is being stretched

gdep-05-c3.text: G. R. Foulger (2007). The “Plate” model for the genesis of melting anomalies. Geophysical Research Abstracts (EGU General Assembly 2007).
gdep-05-c3.quote: most presentday “hot spots” erupt either on or near spreading ridges or in continental rift zones and intraplate regions observed or predicted to be extending
gdep-05-c3.claim: most present-day hotspots erupt on or near spreading ridges or in rifts and other regions that are extending

gdep-05-c3.text: Robert A. Duncan, John A. Tarduno, David W. Scholl (2006). Leg 197 synthesis: Southward motion and geochemical variability of the Hawaiian hotspot. Proceedings of the Ocean Drilling Program, Scientific Results.

gdep-05-c3.claim: the Emperor chain formed mainly while the Hawaiian hotspot itself moved south at a rapid 4–5 cm per year, between about 81 and 47 million years ago

gdep-05-c3.text: Robert A. Duncan, John A. Tarduno, David W. Scholl (2006). Leg 197 synthesis: Southward motion and geochemical variability of the Hawaiian hotspot. Proceedings of the Ocean Drilling Program, Scientific Results.
gdep-05-c3.quote: Growing evidence, however, suggests that the bend might instead record variable drift of the Hawaiian hotspot within a convecting mantle.
gdep-05-c3.claim: The bend may record a drifting plume in a convecting mantle as much as a turning plate.

gdep-05-c3.text: W. Jacquelyne Kious, Robert I. Tilling (1996). Hotspots. This Dynamic Earth: The Story of Plate Tectonics (US Geological Survey).
gdep-05-c3.quote: New studies suggest that hotspots are neither deep phenomena nor "fixed" in position over geologic time, as assumed in the popular plume model.

gdep-06-c1.text: Stephen D. Norton. Geologist Richard Oldham's 1906 Paper on Seismic Wave Transmission Establishes the Existence of Earth's Core and Demonstrates the Value of Seismology for Studying the Structure of Earth's Deep Interior. Science and Its Times (Encyclopedia.com).
gdep-06-c1.quote: Iron loses its magnetism at extremely high temperatures such as those believed to exist at the inner core.
gdep-06-c1.claim: A bar magnet cannot explain the Earth's field: iron loses its magnetism at the temperatures of the core.

gdep-06-c1.text: Monica Pozzo, Chris Davies, David Gubbins, Dario Alfè (2012). Thermal and electrical conductivity of iron at Earth's core conditions. Nature.
gdep-06-c1.quote: generated in the liquid iron core by a dynamo running on heat released by cooling and freezing (as the solid inner core grows), and on chemical convection (due to light elements expelled from the liquid on freezing)
gdep-06-c1.claim: The core has three power sources: heat released as the core cools, latent heat released as the solid inner core freezes, and compositional convection.

gdep-06-c1.text: Gary A. Glatzmaier, Paul H. Roberts (1995). A three-dimensional self-consistent computer simulation of a geomagnetic field reversal. Nature.
gdep-06-c1.quote: A three-dimensional, self-consistent numerical model of the geodynamo is described, that maintains a magnetic field for over 40,000 years.
gdep-06-c1.claim: published a self-consistent computer simulation that maintained a magnetic field for over 40,000 simulated years

gdep-06-c1.text: Gary A. Glatzmaier, Paul H. Roberts (1995). A three-dimensional self-consistent computer simulation of a geomagnetic field reversal. Nature.
gdep-06-c1.quote: The model, which incorporates a finitely conducting inner core, undergoes several polarity excursions and then, near the end of the simulation, a successful reversal of the dipole moment.
gdep-06-c1.claim: Their model, which included an electrically conducting inner core, went through several polarity excursions and then, near the end of the run, a complete reversal of the dipole.

gdep-06-c2.text: Monica Pozzo, Chris Davies, David Gubbins, Dario Alfè (2012). Thermal and electrical conductivity of iron at Earth's core conditions. Nature.
gdep-06-c2.quote: We find both conductivities to be two to three times higher than estimates in current use.
gdep-06-c2.claim: They came out two to three times higher than the values then in use.

gdep-06-c2.text: Monica Pozzo, Chris Davies, David Gubbins, Dario Alfè (2012). Thermal and electrical conductivity of iron at Earth's core conditions. Nature.
gdep-06-c2.quote: New estimates indicate that the adiabatic heat flux is 15 to 16 terawatts at the CMB, higher than present estimates of CMB heat flux based on mantle convection
gdep-06-c2.claim: The adiabatic heat flux at the core–mantle boundary rose to 15–16 terawatts, more than the mantle was thought to extract.

gdep-06-c2.text: Kenji Ohta, Yasuhiro Kuwayama, Kei Hirose, Katsuya Shimizu, Yasuo Ohishi (2016). Experimental determination of the electrical resistivity of iron at Earth's core conditions. Nature.
gdep-06-c2.quote: The low electrical resistivity of iron indicates the high thermal conductivity of Earth’s core, suggesting rapid core cooling and a young inner core less than 0.7 billion years old
gdep-06-c2.claim: the low resistivity implied high thermal conductivity, rapid core cooling and an inner core less than 0.7 billion years old

gdep-06-c2.text: Zuzana Konôpková, R. Stewart McWilliams, Natalia Gómez-Pérez, Alexander F. Goncharov (2016). Direct measurement of thermal conductivity in solid iron at planetary core conditions. Nature.
gdep-06-c2.quote: Our measurements place the thermal conductivity of Earth’s core near the low end of previous estimates, at 18–44 watts per metre per kelvin.
gdep-06-c2.claim: found 18–44 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, near the low end of previous estimates, which allows an inner core as old as the dynamo itself

gdep-06-c2.text: Alfred J. Wilson, Dario Alfè, Andrew M. Walker, Christopher J. Davies (2023). Can homogeneous nucleation resolve the inner core nucleation paradox?. Earth and Planetary Science Letters.
gdep-06-c2.quote: The classical theory of nucleation predicts that the core must be undercooled by several hundred K, which is incompatible with estimates of the core’s present-day temperature.
gdep-06-c2.claim: classical nucleation theory says the core needed several hundred kelvin of supercooling, incompatible with its present-day temperature

gdep-06-c2.text: Alfred J. Wilson, Christopher J. Davies, Andrew M. Walker, Dario Alfè (2025). Constraining Earth's core composition from inner core nucleation. Nature Communications.
gdep-06-c2.quote: Here we show, through molecular dynamics simulations, that nucleation from an Fe1−xCx=0.1-0.15 composition is compatible with a range of geophysical constraints.
gdep-06-c2.claim: found that iron with 10–15% carbon is compatible with a range of geophysical constraints

gdep-06-c3.text: Richard K. Bono, John A. Tarduno, Francis Nimmo, Rory D. Cottrell (2019). Young inner core inferred from Ediacaran ultra-low geomagnetic field intensity. Nature Geoscience.
gdep-06-c3.quote: Plausible yet contrasting core thermal conductivity values lead to inner core growth initiation ages that span 2 billion years, from ~0.5 to >2.5 billion years ago.
gdep-06-c3.claim: Thermal models with different plausible conductivities put the onset of inner-core growth anywhere from about 0.5 to more than 2.5 billion years ago.

gdep-06-c3.text: A. J. Biggin, E. J. Piispa, L. J. Pesonen, R. Holme, G. A. Paterson, T. Veikkolainen, L. Tauxe (2015). Palaeomagnetic field intensity variations suggest Mesoproterozoic inner-core nucleation. Nature.
gdep-06-c3.quote: The most prominent and robust transition in the record is an increase in both average field strength and variability that is observed to occur between a billion and 1.5 billion years ago.
gdep-06-c3.claim: found a clear rise in both average field strength and variability between 1 and 1.5 billion years ago

gdep-06-c3.text: Richard K. Bono, John A. Tarduno, Francis Nimmo, Rory D. Cottrell (2019). Young inner core inferred from Ediacaran ultra-low geomagnetic field intensity. Nature Geoscience.
gdep-06-c3.quote: the lowest value yet reported for the geodynamo from extant rocks and more than ten times smaller than the strength of the present-day field
gdep-06-c3.claim: The Ediacaran field was the weakest yet reported from such rocks, more than ten times weaker than today's

gdep-06-c3.text: John A. Tarduno, Rory D. Cottrell, William J. Davis, Francis Nimmo, Richard K. Bono (2015). PALEOMAGNETISM. A Hadean to Paleoarchean geodynamo recorded by single zircon crystals. Science (New York, N.Y.).

gdep-07-c1.text: Miaki Ishii, Adam M. Dziewoński (2002). The innermost inner core of the earth: evidence for a change in anisotropic behavior at the radius of about 300 km. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America.
gdep-07-c1.quote: we propose the existence of an innermost inner core, with a radius of approximately 300 km, that exhibits a distinct transverse isotropy relative to the bulk inner core
gdep-07-c1.claim: about 300 km in radius, with its own distinct anisotropy

gdep-07-c1.text: Miaki Ishii, Adam M. Dziewoński (2002). The innermost inner core of the earth: evidence for a change in anisotropic behavior at the radius of about 300 km. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America.
gdep-07-c1.quote: Since the discovery of the inner core in 1936, no additional spherical subshell of the Earth has been observed.
gdep-07-c1.claim: It was the first new spherical shell proposed in the Earth since Lehmann's discovery in 1936

gdep-07-c1.text: Thanh-Son Phạm, Hrvoje Tkalčić (2023). Up-to-fivefold reverberating waves through the Earth's center and distinctly anisotropic innermost inner core. Nature Communications.

gdep-07-c1.text: Thanh-Son Phạm, Hrvoje Tkalčić (2023). Up-to-fivefold reverberating waves through the Earth's center and distinctly anisotropic innermost inner core. Nature Communications.

gdep-07-c1.claim: they detected waves that bounced along the Earth's diameter up to five times, crossing the inner core again and again

gdep-07-c1.text: Thanh-Son Phạm, Hrvoje Tkalčić (2023). Up-to-fivefold reverberating waves through the Earth's center and distinctly anisotropic innermost inner core. Nature Communications.

gdep-07-c1.claim: with a radius of about 650 km, in which P-waves are about 4% slower at roughly 50° to the rotation axis, surrounded by a weakly anisotropic outer shell

gdep-07-c2.claim: found the inner core sub-rotated at least 0.1° from 1969 to 1971, then super-rotated about 0.29° from 1971 to 1974

gdep-07-c3.text: Wei Wang, John E. Vidale, Guanning Pang, Keith D. Koper, Ruoyan Wang (2024). Inner core backtracking by seismic waveform change reversals. Nature.
gdep-07-c3.quote: Here we compile 143 distinct pairs of repeating earthquakes, many within 16 multiplets, built from 121 earthquakes between 1991 and 2023 in the South Sandwich Islands.
gdep-07-c3.claim: Wei Wang, John Vidale and colleagues assembled 143 pairs of repeating earthquakes, built from 121 South Sandwich Islands earthquakes between 1991 and 2023

gdep-07-c3.text: Wei Wang, John E. Vidale, Guanning Pang, Keith D. Koper, Ruoyan Wang (2024). Inner core backtracking by seismic waveform change reversals. Nature.
gdep-07-c3.quote: demonstrates that the inner core gradually super-rotated from 2003 to 2008, and then from 2008 to 2023 sub-rotated two to three times more slowly back through the same path
gdep-07-c3.claim: Chaining these matches together, they concluded that the inner core super-rotated gradually from 2003 to 2008 and then, from 2008 to 2023, sub-rotated back along the same path two to three times more slowly.

gdep-07-c3.text: John E. Vidale, Wei Wang, Ruoyan Wang, Guanning Pang, Keith Koper (2025). Annual-scale variability in both the rotation rate and near surface of Earth's inner core. Nature Geoscience.

gdep-07-c3.text: John E. Vidale, Wei Wang, Ruoyan Wang, Guanning Pang, Keith Koper (2025). Annual-scale variability in both the rotation rate and near surface of Earth's inner core. Nature Geoscience.
gdep-07-c3.quote: We thus resolve the long-standing debate on whether temporal variability in PKIKP waves results from rotation or more local action near the inner-core boundary: it is tentatively both.
gdep-07-c3.claim: Their verdict on the long-running dispute between rotation and local surface change was that the answer is tentatively both.

gdep-07-c3.text: John E. Vidale, Wei Wang, Ruoyan Wang, Guanning Pang, Keith Koper (2025). Annual-scale variability in both the rotation rate and near surface of Earth's inner core. Nature Geoscience.
gdep-07-c3.quote: The changes near the inner-core boundary most likely result from viscous deformation driven by coupling between boundary topography and mantle density anomalies or traction on the inner core from outer-core convection.
gdep-07-c3.claim: The likely cause is viscous deformation of the inner-core boundary, driven by gravitational coupling with dense regions of the mantle or by drag from convection in the outer core.
